harmonicFunction: F major establishes a warm, intimate tonal center with Curtis Mayfield-style double stops
Chromatic sliding triads (Eb -> E -> F) build tension and release with effortless swagger
C to Bb to F provides a comforting V - IV - I plagal-dominant cadence
Db and Eb borrowed chords (bVI and bVII) introduce haunting modal depth in the turnaround

techniques.name: Hendrix Thumb-Fretted Chords & Hammer-On Embellishments
techniques.description: Using the left-hand thumb over the top of the neck to anchor root notes on the low E string, freeing fingers 1, 2, and 4 to execute hammer-on/pull-off fills.

notes: Wrap the thumb around to fret the 1st fret low E string (F) and 3rd fret (G)
Index finger bars the B and high E strings
Ring and pinky fingers hammer on 2nd and 4th scale degrees into major triads
Blend rhythm and lead into a seamless, conversational flow
sequence: Fret C chord with bass note on 3rd fret A string, hammering 5th fret D string
Slide down to Bb, executing a 3rd-to-5th fret hammer-on on the G string
Land on F major with thumb over the neck, hammering from open to 2nd fret G string
Add delicate pick-hand grace notes across the treble strings
tips: Lower your thumb slightly behind the neck only when playing wide chord stretches
Relax the fret-hand wrist to allow fingers 2, 3, and 4 to arc freely
Use a light touch with the pick—Hendrix's ballads depend on nuanced dynamic shading

techniques.name: Hybrid Major/Minor Pentatonic Expressive Soloing
techniques.description: Jimi Hendrix's lyrical soloing approach, weaving between sweet F major pentatonic vocal lines and stinging F minor blues bends.

notes: Target the major 3rd (A) on the 10th fret B string for sweet melodic resolution
Incorporate microtonal 'blues curls' between the minor 3rd (Ab) and major 3rd
Execute double-stops across the G and B strings for thick R&B harmonic texture
Control vibrato with gentle finger oscillations rather than wide aggressive wobbles
sequence: Begin with an octave slide into the 10th fret D string (C note)
Play sweet F major pentatonic thirds on strings 2 and 3 at frets 8 and 10
Bend 10th fret G string up a half-step into the major 3rd with delicate vibrato
Cascade down the scale into the chromatic turnaround chords (Db -> Eb -> F)
tips: Switch to the neck pickup on a Stratocaster for warm, hollow, bell-like tone
Roll guitar volume back to 7 or 8 to clean up amp gain into edge-of-breakup
Listen to vocal melodies—Hendrix conceived his solo phrases like sung words

sections.name: Chromatic Sliding Triad Intro
sections.description: The immortal introductory riff, sliding whole triads up by half steps from Eb through E to F.
sections.progression: Eb - E - F - Eb - E - F
notes: Play partial 3-string triad shapes on strings 2, 3, and 4
Slide crisply from 5th/6th fret (Eb) through 6th/7th fret (E) to 7th/8th fret (F)
Let the final F chord ring with a gentle low F bass strike

sections.name: Hendrix Thumb-Over Verse & Embellishments
sections.description: Hendrix's rhythm guitar mastery on display—thumb-anchored bass notes with graceful hammer-on fills decorating C, Bb, and F.
sections.progression: C - Bb - F - C - Bb - F
notes: Play C with thumb muting low E, adding a quick hammer-on on the D string
Slide down to Bb with a smooth hammer-on on the G string
Arrive at F with the thumb fretting fret 1 on the low E string

sections.name: Tender Minor Subdominant Verse Resolution
sections.description: The progression moves through G and Bb before stepping through Db and Eb to resolve back home on F as the vocal sings 'The wind cries Mary'.
notes: G major provides an unexpected secondary dominant lift (V of V)
Bb steps up through borrowed bVI (Db) and bVII (Eb)
Staccato triad strikes into the gentle F resolution

sections.name: Chromatic Riff Re-Entry
sections.description: The signature Eb - E - F sliding triads return between verses, acting as a structural anchor and musical breath.
sections.progression: Eb - E - F - Eb - E - F
notes: Light pick attack with snappy wrist flick
Ensure all three strings in each triad slide in perfect synchronization
Sets up the intimate second verse with quiet dynamic control

sections.name: Expressive Major/Minor Blues Solo
sections.description: One of the most tasteful and expressive guitar solos in classic rock—warm neck pickup tone, singing whole-step bends, and Curtis Mayfield double stops.
sections.progression: F - Eb - Bb - Ab - F - Eb - Bb - Ab - G - Bb - Db - Eb - F
notes: Solo played over descending chords F -> Eb -> Bb -> Ab
Gentle, vocal vibrato oscillating at the peak of bent notes
Blend of F major pentatonic sweetness and F minor blues grit
Tonal warmth achieved through the Stratocaster neck pickup with slight tube compression

sections.name: Final Verse & Floating Outro Chord
sections.description: The song draws to a close with a quiet, poetic final verse, culminating in delicate sliding triads and a shimmering, floating F major chord.
sections.progression: G - Bb - Db - Eb - F (fade out)
notes: Let the final notes ring with natural room ambience
Gentle pick-hand rake across the strings on the final chord
Concludes with an open, wistful sustain that embodies the poem's lyricism

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster (1965 Reissue or American Vintage)
guitar.pickup: Neck single-coil pickup for sweet, glassy, bell-like R&B warmth

amp.recommended: Marshall Super Lead 100W or Fender Twin Reverb

effects.distortion: Clean edge-of-breakup tube tone (guitar volume rolled back to 7.5)
effects.other: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face (used very subtly on the solo with rolled-off volume)

beginner.title: Sliding Triads & Open Position Chords
steps: Learn the 3-string triad shapes on strings 2, 3, and 4
Practice the chromatic slide (Eb -> E -> F) cleanly at 80 BPM
Master the basic C, Bb, and F chord changes without hesitations
Strum gently on quarter notes matching the 80 BPM tempo

intermediate.title: Thumb-Over Technique & R&B Fills
steps: Work on wrapping the left thumb over to fret the low E string notes
Execute hammer-on embellishments on the D and G strings while chords ring
Practice the Db and Eb modal turnaround walkup cleanly
Control right-hand dynamics for sweet, vocal expression

advanced.title: The Full Hendrix Ballad Solo & Touch Control
steps: Learn the note-for-note solo combining major pentatonic and blues bends
Master microtonal pitch bends and singing finger vibrato
Dial in authentic Strat neck-pickup tone with guitar volume control
Perform the entire piece seamlessly blending rhythm and lead

commonMistakes: Strumming too aggressively—this is an intimate ballad that requires dynamic delicacy
Muting adjacent strings when executing hammer-on embellishments
Playing the solo too fast or with overly sharp blues bends instead of vocal vibrato
Struggling with the thumb-over grip—adjust guitar strap height to let the thumb wrap naturally
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Thumb-over fret-hand flexibility and stretching exercises
10 mins: Slow precision practice of the Eb -> E -> F sliding triads
10 mins: Practicing hammer-ons over the C, Bb, and F chord shapes
15 mins: Isolating phrases from the guitar solo with pitch-accurate vibrato
10 mins: Playing through the full track with gentle, conversational dynamics
focusAreas: Left-hand thumb position and finger independence
Synchronization across strings during parallel triad slides
Vocal-style microtonal blues bending and delicate vibrato
Touch sensitivity on pick attack and guitar volume control
metronomeWork: Set click to 80 BPM on beats 2 and 4 to internalize the relaxed groove
Practice sliding triads at 60 BPM ensuring clean pitch transitions
Drill solo double-stops at half speed before playing at performance tempo
